users.description: Users affected, over all its events.

Activity.description: Requests or jobs over the range.

mute_events.description:
With `mute`: until this many more events came; the last of them
brings it back.

started.description: For a missed run, when it should have started.

status.description:
`in_progress`, `ok`, `error`, `missed` (expected, never started) or
`timeout` (did not finish in time).

environment_id.description: The one stage the key sends to; none for a key of the whole project.

name.description: What it is for, such as `claude on my laptop`.

dsn.description: The DSN for the Sentry SDK: `SENTRY_LARAVEL_DSN`.

secret.description: The key itself, shown this once.

mcp_url.description: Logdock's MCP endpoint, for `claude mcp add`.

secret.description: The token itself, shown this once.

Errors.description: Error events over the range, and their issues.

bucket_seconds.description: Whole hours: events are counted per hour.

regressed.description: Came back in the range after they were resolved.

top.description: The issues with the most events in the range; muted ones left out.

contexts.description: The payload's contexts (runtime, os, trace, …), redacted.

exceptions.description: Oldest cause first; the last one was thrown.

frames.description: The stack of an event without an exception.
Oldest call first; the last frame is where it was thrown.

problems.description:
What keeps Logdock from taking data: `database_unavailable`,
`low_disk`, `writer_stalled`.

key_id.description: The key that was used; `null` for requests no key let in.

skipped.description: Items of kinds Logdock does not keep.

resolved_in_next_release.description: Resolved in the release after this one.

hours.description: Events per hour of the last 14 days, oldest first.

oneOf.description: The latest event, kept with the issue.

users.description:
The users affected: the different values of its events' `user` tag,
which the SDK sends only with `send_default_pii`.

environment_id.description:
The one stage the key sends to; none: the stage its data names in
`environment`, added to the project the first time.

attributes.description: The attributes, flattened (`user.id`), in the order they were sent.

time.description: When it was written, RFC 3339 with microseconds.

next.description: Pass as `before` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

next_run.description: When the next run should start.

schedule.description: A crontab (`0 3 * * *`) or `every 10 minute`; `null` without one.

failing.description: Failing or missed, as they are now.

slowest_routes.description:
The routes with the slowest p95, and those with the most failed
requests.

Performance.description: When requests, jobs and queries become performance issues.

job_ms.description: A queued job slower than this; `null` is off.

n_plus_one.description: The same query run again and again in a row (N+1).

overrides.description: Single routes or jobs with a threshold of their own.

request_ms.description: A request slower than this many milliseconds; `null` is off.

slow_query_ms.description: A single SELECT slower than this; `null` is off.

Problem.description: Error body as defined by RFC 9457 (`application/problem+json`).

code.description: Stable, machine-readable identifier the frontend relies on, e.g. `not_found`.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation, if there is more to say than the title.

title.description: Reason phrase of the status code.

processed.description: Jobs that ran from it; of them, those that failed and the retries.

published.description: Jobs put into it by the requests, jobs and commands measured.

allowed_keys.description: When set, only these attribute keys are kept; `user.*` keeps a prefix.

extra_keys.description:
More key fragments whose values are never stored, beyond the built-in
ones (password, token, secret, …).

events.description:
Error events in it, the issues they belong to, and the issues that
first appeared in it.

first_seen.description: When its first and last error or request was seen.

oneOf.description: Its requests (measured with tracing): count, failures, durations.

cookies.description: The cookies' names; their values are never kept.

data.description: The body (form fields, JSON), redacted; a large one is left out.

headers.description:
All headers; secret ones (Authorization, Cookie, CSRF tokens) and
those the redaction rules match read `[redacted]`.

buckets.description: Every bucket of the range, oldest first.

csrf_token.description: Sent back in `X-CSRF-Token` with every request that changes something.

expires_at.description: When the session ends unless used before.

notify.description:
Who gets e-mail about the project's errors, also people without an
account.

code.description: The code Logdock wrote to its log at the start.

needed.description:
No account exists yet: the first administrator is to be created with
the setup code from Logdock's log.

Stats.description: What a range of one name adds up to.

flagged.description:
Failed requests, jobs, commands, queries or outgoing requests; for
the cache, misses.

p50_ms.description: Estimated from a histogram of durations.

max_storage_bytes.description: Above this, the oldest days are deleted; 0 for no limit.

min_free_bytes.description: Below this much free space ingest is refused.

public_url.description: The address SDKs and forwarders send to.

complete.description:
False once an issue keeps no more values of the tag: there may be
more than `distinct`.

distinct.description: Different values; for `user`, the users affected.

key.description:
`user`, `transaction`, `url`, `release`, `browser`, `client_os`,
`service`, `host`, `server_name`, `handled`, `runtime`, or a tag of
the app's own.

recipients.description: How many addresses it went to.

ms.description: Milliseconds; 0 turns it off for this one.

name.description: A route as Logdock names it (`POST /payments`) or a job's class.

logs.description: The trace's log entries, oldest first (at most 500).

transactions.description:
The requests, jobs and commands of the trace, oldest first; a job
continues the trace of the request that queued it.

session.name: __Host-logdock_session
session.description: Set by sign-in or setup. Named `logdock_session` where secure cookies are off.

token.description: An API token (`ldt_…`) from the profile page. It acts for its account and reads everything a session does; it changes nothing but, with the `triage` scope, issues' state. No CSRF token is needed.
